data.ruling: The refutation stands for the blanking part of V287's value. The thresholds (750 counts of 40 uV, 250 counts, INA228 24,000 counts of 1.25 uV) and the latching settings (CEN 0 and WEN 0, which are the reset state) re-derive, and the verifier does not dispute them. The 5 ms blanking does not hold from the maker's datasheet. Its margins are "longer than one INA3221 refresh (3.3 ms typ, 3.63 ms max), shorter than two (6.6 ms typ)". Both assume that in transparent mode an over-limit conversion holds the Critical pin low until the same channel converts again. SBOS576C does not state this. Section 7.3.2.1 says only that the pin "pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit". Table 8-34 defines CEN 0 only as "Transparent (default)". Section 9.2 and Figure 9-2 show one enabled channel, "Enabled channel CH1", so they cannot show how three channels share the pin. Nothing in the datasheet rules out the verifier's case. There, the pin follows each conversion of any channel. A sustained overcurrent on one of three shunt-only channels would then hold the pin low for 1.1 ms typ, 1.21 ms max, in every 3.3 ms cycle. That never exceeds 5 ms, so the 3.0 A abort never fires. Secondary sources, which are not the maker's datasheet, leave the question open. On TI E2E thread 807608, a TI engineer says a transparent pin "should restore automatically after one conversion", without saying which channel's conversion. In the same thread a user measured the Ch.1 critical pin "active for 50ms (6 channels sampled x 8.24ms)", which fits the hold-until-same-channel model, but the post does not state the alert mode. On thread 1625525, a TI engineer says the transparent alert "clears as soon as the shunt voltage drops back down below the programmed level", without a multi-channel case. The pin's release timing with three channels enabled is therefore not read from any maker document, and the value presents a blanking margin that rests on it. Under the page's rules that figure is written as not read, not derived. Scope is function: the finding concerns V287's blanking requirement for the Port current monitor and its configuration, not the INA3221's lifecycle or identity.
data.evidence: SBOS576C (revised September 2026), 7.3.2.1: "The Critical alert pin pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit present in the corresponding-channel critical-alert limit register." No sentence states when the pin releases. Table 8-34: bit 10 CEN "Critical alert latch enable ... 0 = Transparent (default), 1 = Latch enabled"; CF1-3 "cleared when the Mask/Enable register is read back"; nothing on pin release. 7.4.2.1: with shunt only on 3 channels, "two conversions" pass before the device converts the same channel again. 6.5 tCONVERT CT=100: 1.1 ms typ, 1.21 ms max, no minimum. 9.2.1 Table 9-1: "Enabled channel CH1"; Figure 9-2 shows a single channel at 1.1 ms. A full-text search of the datasheet for until/clears/release/deassert finds no release condition for the Critical or Warning pin in transparent mode. The only "until the interrupt is cleared" is in 7.5.3, SMBus alert response, which requires Latch mode. TI E2E 807608, TI engineer: "If the Critical pin is set to transparent mode, after the over limit condition is removed, the Critical pin should restore automatically after one conversion." The same thread's user: "The Critical flag (Ch.1) remains active for 50ms (6 channels sampled x 8.24ms)", alert mode not stated. TI E2E 1625525, TI engineer: transparent alerts "actively change state with the signal ... As soon as the shunt voltage drops back down below the programmed level, the alert clears." Neither TI statement addresses three enabled channels.
